newsitem.title: USA: Quality Dining takes one-time charge, posts loss.
newsitem.headline: Quality Dining takes one-time charge, posts loss.

text.p: Quality Dining, Inc. Wednesday reported a quarterly loss as it took a one-time $8 million pretax charge to restructure operations and acquire Bruegger's Corp., the nation's largest fresh bagel bakery chain.

The Mishawaka, Ind.-based company, which operates and franchises 490 quick service and casual theme restaurants, posted a loss of $2.9 million, or 23 cents a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 4. It had profits of $1.8 million, or 27 cents a share, in the year-ago period.

Revenues rose 148 percent to a record $63.6 million from $25.6 million, driven by the acquisitions of Bruegger's in June and Grady's American Grill, as well as continued strong growth in the company's other businesses.

As of Aug. 4, the company operated 80 Bruegger's Bagel Bakeries and franchised 279 units. It also operates 42 Grady's American Grill restaurants, owns five Spageddies Italian Kitchen restaurants and operates 63 Burger King restaurants and 21 Chili's Grill & Bar restaurants as a franchisee.
At the end of the second quarter, Quality Dining had only 150 restaurants.

"Our record revenues for the quarter and for the fiscal year reflect the initial phase of our commitment to significant growth as a leading restaurant company," said Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Daniel B. Fitzpatrick.

"Our acquisition of Bruegger's should significantly enhance our growth opportunities. As the Bruegger's division grows, it should be the driving force on revenue and income generation for our company."
Quality Dining's stock edged up 56.25 cents to $29 on Nasdaq in late morning trading.
